title: Fifteen Minutes Around the Block: How Movement Lifts a Bad Mood
title_zh: 绕街区走十五分钟：运动如何赶走坏心情
intro_zh: 本文约551词，面向CET-4水平读者。文章从一次心情糟糕的早晨说起，介绍运动改善情绪的化学原理、2018年涉及120多万人的大型研究数据、户外散步的好处、减轻紧张、增强自信与注意力，并给出容易坚持的开始方法。重点词6个：chemical、anxiety、release、tension、confidence、concentration。

paragraphs.en: Imagine this: it is 9 a.m., you have spilled coffee on your shirt and missed the bus. Your mood is low and the day looks ruined. Instead of sitting down to worry, you put on your shoes and walk around the block for fifteen minutes. When you come back, something has shifted. The problem is still there, but it feels smaller. That change is not an accident — it is your brain responding to movement.
paragraphs.zh: 想象一下：早上九点，你把咖啡洒在了衬衫上，还错过了公交车。你心情低落，觉得这一天全毁了。与其坐下来发愁，你换上鞋子，绕着街区走了十五分钟。回来的时候，有些东西已经变了。问题依然在那里，但它看起来变小了。这种变化并非偶然——它是你的大脑对运动作出的反应。

paragraphs.en: Scientists have known for decades that movement changes the chemical mix in the brain. When you exercise, your body produces endorphins, natural painkillers that create calm and even pleasure. Levels of dopamine and serotonin, two messengers linked to mood, also rise, while cortisol, a stress hormone, falls. In short, exercise works like a mild medicine your body makes for itself.
paragraphs.zh: 几十年来科学家已经知道，运动会改变大脑中的化学物质组合。当你运动时，身体会分泌内啡肽——一种天然镇痛物质，能带来平静甚至愉悦感。与情绪相关的两种信使物质多巴胺和血清素的水平也会上升，而压力激素皮质醇则下降。简而言之，运动就像是你身体为自己制造的一剂温和良药。

paragraphs.en: The evidence is stronger than many people expect. In a large study published in 2018, researchers examined the exercise habits and mental health of more than 1.2 million American adults. Those who exercised regularly reported about 43 percent fewer days of poor mental health than those who did not. The best results came from moderate activity — brisk walking, cycling or swimming — for 30 to 60 minutes, three to five times a week.
paragraphs.zh: 证据比许多人想象的更有力。在2018年发表的一项大型研究中，研究者考察了120多万美国成年人的运动习惯与心理健康状况。与不运动的人相比，经常运动的人报告的心理状况不佳的天数大约少了43%。效果最好的是中等强度的活动——快走、骑车或游泳——每次30到60分钟，每周三到五次。

paragraphs.en: The most encouraging finding: you do not need a gym. Dancing in the living room, gardening, walking the dog or taking the stairs all count. A single ten-minute walk can lift a low mood for a couple of hours. The key is not intensity but regularity: the brain rewards movement that happens often, not movement that happens rarely and hurts.
paragraphs.zh: 最令人鼓舞的发现是：你不需要健身房。在客厅里跳舞、种花除草、遛狗或者爬楼梯都算数。仅仅一次十分钟的散步，就能让低落的心情好转几个小时。关键不在于强度，而在于规律：大脑奖励的是经常发生的运动，而不是偶尔一次、还让人难受的运动。

paragraphs.en: Where you exercise matters too. Studies on green exercise show that walking in a park, along a river or under trees eases anxiety more than the same walk on a treadmill indoors. Sunlight helps the body set its internal clock, and green space seems to slow racing thoughts. You do not need a mountain; a few trees and open sky are enough.
paragraphs.zh: 运动的地点也很重要。关于“绿色运动”的研究显示，在公园里、河边或树下散步，比在室内跑步机上走同样的距离更能减轻焦虑。阳光能帮助身体校准生物钟，而绿色空间似乎能让纷乱的思绪慢下来。你不需要一座大山，几棵树和一片开阔的天空就足够了。

paragraphs.en: Exercise also gives the body a way to release tension. Stress often appears as tight shoulders, a fast heartbeat and restless sleep. Moving burns off that extra energy, so muscles relax and the mind settles. Many people fall asleep faster on the days they exercise — and better sleep protects the mood of the next day.
paragraphs.zh: 运动还给身体提供了一条释放紧张的途径。压力常常表现为肩膀发紧、心跳加快和睡眠不安。运动会消耗掉多余的能量，于是肌肉放松、心绪安定。许多人在运动的日子里入睡更快——而更好的睡眠又会守护第二天的情绪。

paragraphs.en: Then there is the quiet effect on confidence. Finishing a run, a swim or even a short workout is small proof that you can do hard things. Over weeks, these wins build a stronger self-image. Team sports add another benefit: company. Playing basketball with friends mixes movement with laughter, and social contact is itself a powerful protector of mental health.
paragraphs.zh: 还有它对自信心的那种安静的影响。跑完一段路、游完一趟泳，甚至只是完成一次短训练，都是“你能做到难事”的小小证明。几周下来，这些小小的胜利会塑造出更强大的自我形象。团队运动还带来另一个好处：陪伴。和朋友打篮球把运动与笑声结合起来，而社交本身就是心理健康强有力的保护因素。

paragraphs.en: You may also notice that your concentration improves. After a short walk or bike ride, the brain receives more oxygen and more of a protein called BDNF, which helps brain cells grow and connect. Exercise cannot replace medicine or professional help for serious depression, but doctors increasingly treat it as a useful partner.
paragraphs.zh: 你可能还会发现自己的专注力提高了。在短暂散步或骑车之后，大脑会获得更多氧气和一种名为BDNF的蛋白质，它有助于脑细胞生长与连接。对于严重的抑郁症，运动不能替代药物或专业帮助，但医生越来越把它视为一位有用的伙伴。

paragraphs.en: So how do you start? Make it very small: five minutes of stretching, one song of dancing, one stop earlier on the bus. Attach it to something you already do — after lunch, or before your evening shower. The goal is not to become an athlete. It is to give your mood a simple, free tool that is always within reach.
paragraphs.zh: 那么该如何开始呢？把它变得非常小：拉伸五分钟、跳完一首歌、提前一站下车。把它挂在你已经习惯的事情上——午饭后，或者晚上洗澡前。目标不是成为运动员，而是给你的情绪一件简单、免费、随时可用的工具。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Exercise is useful only for people who want to become athletes.
Regular physical activity can improve mood through chemical, physical and social effects.
Serious depression should be treated mainly by running every day.
Team sports are the only effective way to feel happier.
questions.explain: 全文从化学机制、2018年大型研究、户外运动、缓解紧张、增强自信与专注等角度说明运动能改善情绪，故B为正确答案。A、C过于绝对，D把团队运动说成唯一方式，均与原文不符。

questions.q: According to the study published in 2018, people who exercised regularly reported ______.
options: about 43 percent fewer days of poor mental health
no change in their mental health at all
more days of poor mental health than non-exercisers
that only intense exercise helped them
questions.explain: 细节题。第三段明确指出，经常运动的人报告心理状况不佳的天数比不运动的人少约43%，故选A。B、C与原文相反，D与原文“中等强度效果最好”矛盾。

questions.q: What can be inferred about starting to exercise from the last paragraph?
options: You should buy expensive equipment first.
You must exercise for at least an hour every day.
Beginning with very small amounts makes it easier to keep going.
Exercise only works if you do it at a gym.
questions.explain: 推断题。末段建议“把它变得非常小”，如拉伸五分钟、跳一首歌、提前一站下车，并把它挂在已有习惯上，可见从小量开始更容易坚持，故选C。A、B、D在文中均无依据。

questions.q: In Paragraph 6, the word 'release' is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.explain: 词义题。第六段说运动让身体“release tension”，后文提到肌肉放松、心绪安定，说明release意为“释放、放掉”，与let go of最接近。hold back（抑制）、add to（增加）、hide away（藏起）均与语境不符。
